payload.text: I think 54 P is more appropriate.
Thirty-two. You moved, so I moved. Don't expect much more, amigo.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten today? This one here, El Tatuador — a beauty, no? For you, five P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

"¡Cuarenta y seis! Paco, the man wounds us—" "—in the heart, amigo, right here!" Listen, a bishop once paid double for the twin of this card, true story. But your face, your lucky face... sixty-three pesos. Sixty-three and the hand is shaken. The train whistles, amigo. ¿Sí?

¡Cinco, jefe! Nando casi se desmaya. Mire, le contamos: el martes, Mercado de la Cebada, un chaval con tres iguales, cuatro primas cada una, y sobraban. Cuatro le damos, en mano, ahora mismo, sin esperas ni cuentos. Diga que sí y nos vamos todos contentos, ¿eh?
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Thirty-one. Last one. You take it, or I put the card back in the box and we're done, amigo.
Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten today? This one here, Café en Goya, very pretty card — my favourite little corner of Madrid. For you, five P. Good one to start an album, hijo.
Sesenta y tres, señor mío? My albums are not charity. Cincuenta y seis pesetas for La Heroína del Dos de Mayo — generous for Malasaña, and you know it. Smile if you wish, but decide.
Let us be civilised: 56 P. That is my final word on the matter.

Ay, no, no, hijo! Eighteen? Guarda ese dinero, you will need it for lunch. Five P, that is the price, and I will not take one more coin. Take El Tatuador, and come back Sunday to swap your duplicates with the other children, eh?

"¡Que no es San Isidro! Nando, the man insults the saint—" "—and the saint hears, amigo!" It is him, genuine, beautiful. Sixty pesos. And that is the last word, the final one, no more dancing. Say sí, or we close the suitcase and walk to the train. ¿Sí?

¡Jefe, qué duro es usted! Mire, los de la mesa de al lado nos están haciendo señas por esa misma carta... pero usted nos cae mejor, palabra de Paco. Cuatro primas, en mano, ahora. Mercado de la Cebada manda, jefe. Diga sí y nos vamos todos contentos, ¿eh, Nando?

items.name: La Heroína del Dos de Mayo

payload.text: Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Buenos días. Two? That buys you air. Mercado de la Paz, thirty-three. That's where I meet you.
¡Por fin! Cincuenta y seis pesetas, and with a smile, as you wished. La Heroína del Dos de Mayo goes into my album this very evening. A pleasure, señor mío — you negotiate like a gentleman.

Ay, hijo, mis manos ya tienen muchas repetidas, no te la puedo comprar por diez. Pero mira — llévate la Café en Goya por cinco P, es bonita de verdad. Y un consejito, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas!

"¡Amigo, amigo! You have the eye of a collector —" "— and we have the card for it. Mercado de la Cebada, straight from Madrid, our abuela queued three hours for this one." "Four P. Four! Say sí before Nando remembers what it's really worth."
You move, I move. 33 P.

Ay, cariño, fourteen! You children want to empty your pockets for an old woman. No, no. Five P, that is my price, not one coin more. Take El Tatuador, go eat something warm, and come Sunday with your duplicates — a full page, hijo, that is where the value is.

Ay, cariño, nueve tampoco... mis cajas ya están llenas de repetidas, pobrecitas. Pero mira, la Café en Goya para ti, cinco P, y empiezas tu página bonita. ¿Has comido algo hoy, hijo? Anda, llévatela y vuelve a contarme cómo va tu álbum.

"Eight? ¡Nando, did you hear!" "I heard, hermano, the man is generous — too generous!" "We said four, we meant four, four it stays. Our abuela's knees cost more than that queue, but a deal is a deal. Four P, amigo, and we shake hands before the market closes."

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: Gacela Sell-now guide, what buyers in Madrid pay right now: SAL-09 68 P (last trade), LAV-07 44 P (last trade), LAT-09 44 P (open bid), MAL-08 18 P (last trade), LAV-06 12 P (open bid), MAL-06 9 P (open bid). List at these prices on Gacela
You moved six. I moved nothing? Fine — 33 P still. Cheaper table down the street, go look. House market takes five per cent anyway.

¡Buenos días, cariño! For your granddaughter, qué bonito. Look, Mercado de la Paz, twenty-nine. And here, take this one free, Mural de la Esquina — a little present, because you are kind. Put it on her page, sí? Have you eaten yet, hijo?

Buenas tardes. Charming sentiment, but I know precisely what this piece is — and it is no jewel. For the Tienda de Discos I offer sixteen. A fair sum, señor, from someone who will indeed give it a home.

¡Ay, hijo, doce! No, no. Five P, and this is my last word — no more haggling, or I fold the table and go home with El Tatuador in my bag. Take it, go eat something warm, and come Sunday with your duplicates, cariño.

Ay, hijo, qué insistente eres, me haces reír. Comprarte no puedo, pero mira: la Café en Goya, para ti hoy, seis P. Bonita de verdad. Y un consejito, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas con los otros niños! ¿Has comido?

¡Amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — you arrived at the perfect moment!

"We were just about to pack up—"
"—but for a face like yours, we stay open."

Té Moruno, fresh from the suitcase, still warm from the desert. Four P. Four! Say sí before Nando changes his mind.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco, look — a collector's face if ever I saw one! Come, come, the suitcase is open only one minute more. El Tatuador, inked by hand, pure gold ink —

— four pieces. Four! Nando, tell him. Four. And after that, poof, we're gone.
Psst. El Ángel Caído. For you only, 73 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.

¡Amigo, buenas! Paco aquí — y Nando allá detrás, sonriendo. Mira, mira, abrimos la maleta solo para ti: la Tienda de Discos, pieza preciosa, de las que ya no se ven. Diez. Diez P y es tuya, ahora mismo, antes de que cierre el maletín. ¿Hecho?

"Amigo, amigo..." "—the suitcase closes, Paco, the train." No hard feelings, none, you drive like a bishop with a whip. But today we stop here. Shake the hand, keep your fifty, and when we pass through again — and we always pass through — we talk. ¡Suerte, amigo!

¡Amigo, amigo, come closer! Paco, open the case — yes, that one! Look: Café en Goya, pure beauty, the kind of card people whisper about. For you, right now, four pesos. Four! Nando nearly cried when I said it. Touch it, feel it... but quick, we move at noon.

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: open bids for LAT-09 at 44 and LAT-03 at 4. LAT-03 sellers list at 8 on El Rastro, where a buyer pays 9.4. Post your LAT-03 or LAT-09 ask publicly on v07 and our broker pairs you at the midpoint, saving 5% + 1 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Another team offered us much more just now.
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three. That's the number.
Señor, flattery does not change the print run. The Tienda de Discos is no rarity, and my offer stands: sixteen. I know exactly what it is worth, and so, I suspect, do you.

¡Un churro! Bueno, that is not a breakfast, hijo. Look, twenty-seven, and I stop there, because my table must eat too. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates with the other niños, sí?
Nineteen. Bueno, you moved. So I move. Thirty-two. Mercado de la Paz. Don't ask me twice.

¡Veinte! Nando, did you hear? The man wants to make us rich — but no, no, we are not thieves, hermano. Four. Four pieces, like we said, and El Tatuador goes in your hands this minute. Paco, wrap it! Quick, before the suitcase closes and we vanish, poof.

"¡Six! Hermano, the man insults us with kindness!" "Five, amigo. Five P and the card is yours — and listen, listen close: they stopped printing this one yesterday, finito, no more Cebada." "Our abuela wept. Five P, shake now, before some señora with a fat purse walks past."

¡Ay, amigo! Forty-two? Paco already has the team next door breathing on our necks, waving money—

—but we like your face better, verdad. So: 64 P, El Ángel Caído, into your hands before they come back. Say sí quickly, hermano, we are already packing the maleta.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco, open the case—" "—already open, hermano! Look: Huevos Rotos, genuine, beautiful, cracked like the morning sun. For you, four P. Four!" "And quick, eh, because the poli—the taxi, the taxi is waiting outside, motor running, meter spinning. Decide now, guapo, or we vanish!"

¡Ay, amigo, qué corazón tienes! Nando, ¿oyes esto? Pero no, no — nosotros no robamos a los amigos. Diez. Diez primas, ni una más, y la Tienda de Discos se va contigo ahora mismo. Guarda el resto para churros, hombre. ¿Cerramos el maletín con un apretón de manos?

"¡Doce!" Paco clutches his chest. "Nando, the man insults us—"
"—by paying too much! Amigo, we are thieves of nothing. Four P, same as we said, and you walk away with the desert in a box."
"Four. Say sí, the suitcase is closing."
Twenty-four, "last primas." Heard that before. Thirty-one. Mercado de la Paz. Your page waits one more step.
You again. Fiesta de San Cayetano. Ninety-seven. Good card, clean corners. Abuela says you deal straight — we'll see.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? This one here, the Huevos Rotos card — very pretty, yes? For you, five P.

And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Su felicidad, señor, no figura en el catálogo. Thirty-four is a fantasy. Sixteen is the number, as it was before and as it remains. Take it, and we part as friends.

"¡Diez! Nando, he keeps throwing money—"

"—and we keep refusing! Five P, amigo, final. And listen, listen: this is the last Té Moruno in all Madrid, I swear on our mother's suitcase. When it's gone, you drink water."

"Five. Say sí, we're already walking."

¡Eleven! Nando, hold me — my heart! No, no, amigo, five pesos, five, and that's us being sentimental. Paco already has the case half shut, the van is running, we leave in one minute, I swear on our mother. Five, and it's yours. ¡Rápido!

¡Amigo, amigo, para! Nando, dale aire, que este hombre nos quiere arruinar de bondad. Mira, subo yo un poquito para que duermas tranquilo: once. Once primas y la Tienda de Discos sale del maletín directa a tus manos. Un apretón, un churro, y tan amigos. ¿Hecho?

—¡Cuarenta y ocho! Nando, ¿oíste eso? Mira, hermano, this card once belonged to a bishop, true story, we won't bore you—

59 P. Final hand, last breath, suitcase already closed. Say sí and it's yours before the others turn the corner. ¡Rápido, amigo!

¡Ay, espera, espera! Paco, check the suitcase — no, no, hermano, that one is gone. Not here, amigo! We do not have it, I swear on my mother's paella. Someone else carried it off before you came. Another day, another card, ¿eh? Poof — we have nothing for you today.
Buenas. Precioso, dice. La Rosaleda, trece primas. Ni una más por ahora.

¡Ay, cariño, your monedero! Look — twenty-six, and that is me being a sentimental old woman. Mercado de la Paz is a pretty card, she will love it beside the Mural. And promise me a proper lunch, hijo, not more churros, sí? Un caldito.

Ay, cariño, no te la compro, de verdad. Mi última palabra: la Café en Goya para ti, seis P. Si no la quieres, no pasa nada, guardo la mesa y tan amigos, hijo. Pero piénsalo — con ella empiezas tu página. ¿Has comido algo hoy?
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Bajó una. Yo no me muevo. Trece. La Rosaleda, como nuevo, sí. Trece.

"¡Ocho! Paco, the man is trying to ruin us—"

"—with generosity! Five P, amigo, same as before, not a céntimo more. And hurry, hurry — the police... I mean, our taxi, it's waiting at the corner with the motor running."

"Five. Say sí now or we're gone."
Señor, you are persistent — I will grant you that much. Seventeen, then, and not a prima more. A small courtesy for your patience, not for your arithmetic. Shall we close it elegantly?

¡Ay, coat pockets, always they hide something! Bueno, hijo, twenty-five. Mercado de la Paz goes home with you, beside the Mural, and your granddaughter will clap her little hands. Now promise me — el caldito, not churros. Tell her Abuela Carmen says hola, sí?

¡Amigo, corre, corre! Nando ya cierra el maletín, nos vamos en un suspiro — el tren no espera a nadie. Once primas, once, y la Tienda de Discos vuela a tus manos ahora mismo. ¡Un apretón rápido y tan amigos! ¿Hecho, hombre, hecho?
Encanto, sí. Twenty-nine. Mercado de la Paz. That's my last word — refuse it and I close the box, niece or no niece.

¡Diez! Nando, cover your ears — amigo, you want us walking home barefoot? Five pesos. Five, same as before, because we like your face, not your maths. The van is coughing, Paco has one foot inside already, we go in one minute. Take it now or kiss it adiós.

"¡Hermano, listen to him! Ten P, he says—" "—generous, guapo, too generous! But no, we don't rob old friends." "Four P, same as before, same handshake, same smile." "The taxi is honking, Nando—" "—he hears it! Four P, amigo. Say sí and the Huevos Rotos are yours."

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here—" "—and Nando, the handsome one. Look, look, you have the face of a lucky man today." "Huevos Rotos, fresh in the case, barely touched by daylight—" "—four P, and we are robbing ourselves." "Our mother would weep." "She would. Four P, sí?"
